structure: Part 2, address-book list and view. Read in full: list.fit.spec.js and view.fit.spec.js, and all 11 traces they recorded (list.fit 762a7 navigation, 3e618 table, fe734 add link, 49f4e axe, d7e93 pagination, 964e2 empty state; view.fit 4a433 open from a row, cd84f every field, 2e5d8 Edit and Delete, 4811a Back, 14089 axe). tim's bundled Playwright cannot open these traces (TraceVersionError), so each trace's unzipped contents in this part's working folder were read directly: test.trace for the action list (every action transcribed) and 1-trace.trace for the DOM snapshots, rendered to HTML with jq, plus 1-trace.network for the requests. Pages reached, in order: stub sign-in (302) lands on the Dashboard at / (part 4 owns its content; only the service navigation is claimed here); the Address book list at /address-book (title 'Address book | Import notification service', H1 'Address book', intro line, a Search addresses form, an Add a new address button-link, a 'Showing x-y of z' results label, a table of Name, Address, Country and a visually hidden Action column with a View link per row); the same list at /address-book?page=2 when an organisation has 30 addresses (25 per page, GOV.UK pagination with numbered links, Next and Previous); the empty state for an organisation with no addresses (message, no table, no results label, the Add a new address button still shown); the view address page at /address-book/{id} (title and H1 are the address name, a Back link to /address-book above main, a summary list of nine Standard Address Block rows, then Edit and Delete button-links in a button group). The Add a new address click is followed only as far as the add form's URL and heading; parts 1 and 3 own the add, edit and delete pages. Both pages are entirely govuk-frontend components (service navigation, table, pagination, button, summary list, back link, input, button group). Each page passed an axe check for serious or critical violations. All page loads are server-rendered GETs; no address-book API call is visible from the browser, so the backend integration is recorded as a gap. Search, an unknown address id, ordering rules and pagination beyond two pages were never exercised and are recorded as gaps.

claims.note: The seed ids also run 000…001 to 000…030 in the same order, so the list may be in id or creation order. No test asserts an order.
